note: Simulated review by an AI model; role-separated, not independent. Persuasion-blind: RESPONSE.md (round 3 and round 1) not read. item_id uses roadmap ids, as in Phase 1. precommitment_hash = sha256 over sorted-key compact UTF-8 JSON of phase1_criteria.json. Anchors quote revised/main.tex; macros resolved via revised/numbers.tex; table medians and equivalence counts recomputed from revised/figures/table_cells_*.tex and found consistent with numbers.tex. One external check: the Fortunato et al. 2005 abstract (arXiv physics/0504017). New-issue ids continue from round 2 (NEW-1..3), so this round's run NEW-4..NEW-9.

residual_gap.text: Side-by-side reporting is still incomplete. The gaps in variance, directional dispersion, radial variance, effective groups and convergence time are given only for run-matched thresholds, not for shared, start-matched or early-matched ones (Tables cells-pass and cells-groups cover only the pass rate and the primary outcome). §5 still calls the run-matched design 'recommended' without saying why that estimand is preferred there. The claim that 100 rounds 'ends before most opinion groups have formed' is asserted without supporting numbers.

evidence_anchor: text: §2 Related work, 'Euclidean distance is the usual default for vector opinions \citep{fortunato2005,lorenz2007}'
text: §2, '\citet{flache2017} review social-influence models more widely'
text: §2, 'We describe both models with the ODD protocol \citep{grimm2020}.'

verdicts.change_summary: A dedicated Related-work section now cites in the text all of R2's references, docking/alignment, the BC surveys, flache2017 and grimm2020 (every refs.bib entry is cited), where the original had no such section.

residual_gap.text: Mostly done; two gaps remain. (a) Fortunato et al. 2005 is cited only as support for 'Euclidean distance is the usual default', but by its own abstract that paper tests different shapes of the confidence range (external: https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0504017). It is therefore a direct precedent for comparing distances and is mis-positioned. This is a peripheral made-worse trigger (mis-description) that does not outweigh the progress, so PARTIALLY under the precedence rule. (b) Fortunato 2005, Huet 2008, Kurahashi-Nakamura 2016, Baumann 2021 and Schweighofer 2020 are each described in a list clause, not tied to this paper's argument.

verdicts.change_summary: Per-cell paired-bootstrap CIs for the pass rate and the primary outcome are now printed, margins are justified ahead of the results, and the case null claims are now tested (own-target interaction equivalent at ±0.01; 'no effect' softened to 'little effect'); cosine and angular are still pooled in every 36-case median and count, and the 'one gate'/'common ruler removes' claims still rest on point maxima.

residual_gap.text: (iv) Every summary median and equivalence count (\VRunGroupEquiv of \VCases, \VTzeroPassGap and so on) still pools cosine and angular, the near-duplicates that Lemma 1 says form one gate. (iii) 'Cosine and angular gates are one gate' and the abstract's 'one common ruler removes the difference' still rest on point medians/maxima (0.00, at most 0.07) with no TOST, and Fig. 3a shows that the own-ruler medians (0.08-0.12) are themselves inside the ±0.25 margin. (i) Per-cell CIs exist only for the pass rate and the primary outcome, not for the other reported gaps. (ii) Both margin justifications are tied to observed results (a tenth of the median shared-threshold gap; a third of the recommended interaction). The case margin was set after the round-2 manuscript had already reported the own-target interval it is used to test, so 'fixed before this analysis' should say so. These gaps touch the abstract's ruler claim.

evidence_anchor: text: §5.3, 'The centred cells hold the gate space fixed and vary only the threshold rule.'
text: §5.3, 'with a lag-0 effect of \VCUnitRunGatedCosZero\ against Euclidean's \VCUnitRunGatedEucZero, so a modest change makes a large ratio'
verdicts.change_summary: The centred rows are now named as the comparison that isolates the threshold, with numbers (+0.035/+0.032/+0.034 anchor; +0.015/+0.003/+0.013 gated), §1 is qualified, and the extreme cell (now index 292 on the relative effect) is explained using Euclidean's lag-0 effect.

residual_gap.text: The explanation of the extreme cell is contradicted by its own numbers. With a lag-0 effect of -0.042 and an index of 292, cosine's lag-40 relative effect is about -0.123, a change of about -0.081 against Euclidean's -0.025. Its interaction (-0.057) is the largest-magnitude interaction in Fig. 4. So the change is not 'modest' and the small denominator does not explain the cell; restate it, for example as cosine's lag-40 effect approaching Euclidean's.

new_issues.description: The 'settled' criterion (no move above 1e-4) uses an absolute tolerance that is not rescaled with the cube. §4.1 says Euclidean dynamics are unchanged by shifting and rescaling, so its unit and centred cells are the same 9 designs; yet the Euclidean unsettled shares and convergence times differ between paired unit/centred cells (d=2, c=5%: 66%/31% vs 60%/22%; d=2, c=30%: 523 vs 468 rounds; d=4, c=5%: 92%/67% vs 91%/55%). The per-cell settled table, the pooled 26%/13%/14% and the convergence-time gap therefore depend on the coordinate coding, an instance of the hidden choice the paper warns about.
new_issues.location_anchor: table: Appendix Table settled, centred vs unit Euclidean rows
new_issues.competence_basis: Simulation-methods seat; checked the table against the §4.1 equivariance statement.
new_issues.attribution_evidence: The per-cell settled table and the definition of 'settled' are new in the revision (absent from original/main.tex and original/figures); only pooled Euclidean shares were printed before, so the inconsistency could not be seen in the original.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: R10 asks for per-cell unsettled shares and convergence time to be reported; it does not cover whether the convergence criterion is invariant to the coordinate coding.

new_issues.description: §1 says that 'the threshold, the grouping radius and the stopping time each changed how large the differences between geometries looked'. §5 reports instead that the group gaps 'barely move' from 500 to 4,000 rounds (0.93 to 0.87; 0.71 to 0.70), so the stopping-time part of the claim is contradicted by the paper's own result.

new_issues.non_match_rationale: R14 concerns the threshold part of the §1 size claim for the case; the stopping-time part and its conflict with §5 are not covered.

new_issues.description: The backward design says the audit's changes are undone 'in all eight combinations, and then the trust step'. In Fig. 4, however, the two trust rows pair centre trust with different subsets ('+ tightening tick' and '+ cosine step, random streams', without the tick). Neither is the draft engine with trust alone or with all the other changes, so the reader cannot tell what the trust rows isolate.

new_issues.non_match_rationale: NEW-2 is about the caption/label coding and the rows the text quotes, both now resolved; it does not cover whether the set of trust configurations matches the stated design.

new_issues.description: The terms are used inconsistently across the case description. The glossary defines 'policy pull' as the move toward the perceived policy, but Appendix B separates the policy pull (step 5: anchor or gated, toward the policy p) from a distinct move toward the perceived policy (step 6, from the lag on), and §5.1 mentions only the latter. Separately, 'in each corner of the design' (§5.2) reuses 'corner', which also names a trust target and the cube's corner.
